newsitem.title: UK: OPEC helps world oil prices chart steady course.
newsitem.headline: OPEC helps world oil prices chart steady course.

text.p: The world oil market gave OPEC ministers meeting in Vienna on Wednesday an approving nod as prices for benchmark Brent Blend crude held steady in the face of the resumption of Iraqi exports.

The Brent January contract on the International Petroleum Exchange traded at an intra-day high of $23.02 a barrel but came off after the United Nations reported that arrangements for Iraqi oil sales were in place.
January Brent fell back to close at $22.72 a barrel, just two cents down on the day after U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali reported to the Security Council.
But Boutros-Ghali did not say when he would give the go-ahead for implementing the plan that will allow Iraq to sell $2.0 billion in oil over six months to buy food and medicine.

Iraq's chief delegate at the OPEC meeting in Vienna, Osama al-Hiti, said he expected his country would resume oil sales in a matter of weeks although he said Iraq had not yet signed term contracts with buyers.
Iraqi oil exports have been locked out of the market by U.N. sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) met in Vienna amid general consensus for a six-month rollover of the current output ceiling of 25.03 million bpd, which takes into account Iraq's portion under the "oil-for-food" deal.
Oil prices are on average some $3.0 higher than they were a year ago, having risen in October to a five-year peak of $25.06 a barrel on fears of a supply crunch as demand grew faster than forecast.

But OPEC President and acting UAE Oil Minister Rakad bin Salem bin Rakad cautioned members against taking higher oil prices for granted although he made no mention of overproduction by some OPEC producers.

"The events of the past six months in the international oil market have taken many people by surprise. After a long period of market weakness, we have begun to witness price levels last seen, in regular market conditions, more than a decade ago," Rakad told OPEC's opening session.
This showed that market fundamentals were "sturdier than many analysts had predicted," he added.

Rakad said the rise in oil prices since September, which he said was helped with a stronger dollar and the delay in implementing the Iraqi-U.N. deal, reflected fears within the industry that crude and heating oil products were unusually low in the approach to the northern hemisphere winter.
Additionally, world oil demand was higher and non-OPEC supply lower than predicted, he said.
He told delegates that OPEC should satisfy short and long-term fundamentals and guard against complacency.

"In spite of the present improved conditions, we must guard against taking the situation for granted. As we are well aware, market fortunes can change radically and rapidly in a short space of time," Rakad said.
